[USER] Andrew tells Christina that the meaning of life, the universe and everything is the number 42. After hearing this, Christina says that the ideal number of children she would like to have is 38. What is this probably an example of? (3 pts.)  
[USER] a) Framing effects  
[USER] b) Anchoring effects  
[USER] c) Numerosity effects  
[USER] d) Very odd flirting in a conversation unrelated to human cognition  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] This is probably an example of anchoring effects.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Anchoring effects refer to the tendency to rely too heavily on the first piece of information encountered (the "anchor") when making subsequent judgments or decisions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In this case, Andrew's mention of the number 42 may have served as an anchor for Christina's subsequent response about the number of children she would like to have.  
[USER] Exemplar models of categorization hold that (2 pts.)  
[USER] a) Instances are better categorized when a prototype is calculated  
[USER] b) Instances are better categorized when a prototype is presented  
[USER] c) Instances are less important than prototypes  
[USER] d) Instances are more important than prototypes  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Exemplar models of categorization hold that instances are more important than prototypes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In these models, category membership is determined by the similarity of an instance to previously encountered examples, or exemplars, of the category rather than a prototypical representation.
